title: Bar Tamlon
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Pesikta Rabbati](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesikta_Rabbati.22.1), in the second section on the Ten Commandments (subsection 6 in Hyman’s citation), relates that a man deposited money with Bar Tamlon, who denied receiving it. They came to court, and Bar Tamlon had to swear. He put the money inside a hollow cane and handed the cane to the depositor to hold while he swore, etc. [Nedarim 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nedarim.25a.4-6) tells the well-known story of Rava’s cane, but does not name the man.[^1][^2]

notes.text: Both stories involve money hidden inside a cane passed to the claimant just before an oath. In the Bavli the case comes before Rava, and the borrower is unnamed.
The comparable story in [Pesikta Rabbati 22](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesikta_Rabbati.22.1) names Bar Talmyon (בר תלמיון). Hyman writes Bar Tamlon and gives his own subsection numbering.
